<thought>Using the ESI‑MS spectrum, the most intense ion is at m/z 183.0451, which corresponds to the [M+H]⁺ ion. Subtracting the proton mass gives a neutral monoisotopic mass of ≈182.0378 Da. The isotopic pattern shows a strong M+2 peak (~33 % of the base peak), characteristic of a single chlorine atom (⁷⁵Cl/⁷⁷Cl). Accounting for one ⁽³⁵⁾Cl (34.968852 Da) and solving 12 C + 1.007825 H + 15.994915 O + 34.968852 = 182.0378 yields the formula C₁₀H₁₁OCl, which matches the observed mass within typical instrument tolerance and explains the isotopic distribution.  

The required format is CxHyOzX, where X denotes the non‑C/H/O element (Cl).  

**Molecular formula:** C10H11OCl</thought>
<final_answer>C10H11OCl</final_answer>
